Luxembourg-Japan Double Taxation Convention (as applicable to cross-border trade and procurement)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Trade register or companies registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs and authorized signatories against EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and FSE sanctions lists, Luxembourg FSI/CSSF financial intelligence bulletins, and domestic adverse-media and politically exposed person (PEP) databases. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for any PEP connection, high-risk tax residency, or unusual source-of-funds pattern; all screenings must be documented before incorporation and periodically refreshed under CSSF Regulation No 12-02.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) at https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: RCS filings are accepted in French; the corporate name must be stated in Latin script. Non-Latin or transliterated names must be romanized and, where practicable, accompanied by a French translation or faithful transliteration. The chosen name must respect Luxembourg public order, be sufficiently distinctive, not be misleading as to the object of the company, and must not create confusion with existing RCS-registered names or previously reserved names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A written reconsideration request may be filed with the RCS registration officer through the LBR portal within 15 days of a rejection decision. If the RCS maintains the refusal, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Luxembourg administrative tribunal within three months of notification. Parallel name reservation with an alternative permissible name is available; a newly reserved name is valid for 30 days and no extension is granted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted subject to appointment of a licensed domiciliation agent or physical registered-office provider in Luxembourg; the arrangement must provide a valid administrative seat, mailing address and accessible records. A virtual-office-only structure is acceptable for ISIC 4631 low-risk wholesale distribution subject to adequate economic substance oversight and verifiable management functions in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a non-licensed trading entity; estimated 10% annual probability of an unannounced inspection by the Luxembourg Business Registers or tax administration within the first 24 months, increasing to approximately 35% if VAT registration, bank credit, or Economic Substance Board monitoring is triggered.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 100-110 and 1600-1 et seq. (SARL provisions); Law of 25 September 2017 on Food Safety; Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 on food hygiene; Regulation (EC) No 178/2002
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) deposited with the RCS and published in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed capital EUR 12,000; at least 25% (EUR 3,000) must be effectively paid up into a blocked escrow bank account (compte bloqué) with a Luxembourg or EEA credit institution prior to notarial signature; the blocked funds are released to the company only upon RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST GENERAL MEETING RESOLUTION OF THE SHAREHOLDERS OF [●] SARL, dated [●]: 1. The draft articles of incorporation are approved, establishing the corporate purpose of international wholesale, import and distribution of culinary and ceremonial grade organic matcha powder and allied food products (ISIC 4631). 2. The share capital of EUR 12,000 is subscribed in full by the Shareholder, and the blocked capital account certificate is acknowledged. 3. The registered office is fixed at [●], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. 4. [●] is appointed sole manager (Gérant) with sole signature powers. 5. The Gérant is directed to execute the notarial deed, file with the RCS, publish in the RESA, and apply for the establishment permit, EORI, VAT number and ALVA food-wholesale registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notary engagement, name clearance and opening of blocked capital account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg and Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary and request an advance name verification and negative certificate from the RCS. Simultaneously open a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) in the name of the company in formation with a Luxembourg or EEA credit institution and deposit the minimum paid-up capital of EUR 3,000 (or the full subscribed capital as elected). The notary drafts the articles of incorporation (statuts) and the related shareholders' resolution.
required_dossiers: Negative certificate / name availability clearance from the RCS
Passports or EU identity cards and proof of residential address of each shareholder
Attestation de blocage de fonds (blocked funds certificate) issued by the bank
Draft articles of incorporation (projet de statuts)
LEI (Legal Entity Identifier) application details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, promptly submit alternative names with distinguishing suffixes; if the bank declines the blocked account, obtain a certificate of funds from another EEA credit institution acceptable to the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public registered with the Chambre des Notaires; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders appear in person or by duly appointed proxy before the notary, who verifies identity, legal capacity, capital subscription and payment, and the corporate purpose. The authentic deed (acte constitutif) is read, approved and signed. The notary performs the statutory lien/registry checks, registers the deed with the AEDT for stamp duty, and transmits the file electronically to the RCS for the registration application.
required_dossiers: Final draft of the notarial deed
Blocked funds certificate and underlying bank confirmation
Original identification documents of founders and, if corporate shareholders exist, certified extract of their register and board authorization
Written proxy with apostille or legalization where applicable
Shareholders' written resolution approving the deed and appointment of management
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a founder fails to appear, a new hearing is scheduled within 24-48 hours using an apostilled proxy; if the notary issues a reservation regarding capital payment, the bank statement is refreshed and the deed re-signed without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and publication in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS electronic filing platform (eRCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After execution of the notarial deed, the notary submits the deposit application to the RCS via the eRCS platform. The RCS examines corporate legality, assigns the registre de commerce number (matricule), and issues the certificate of registration. The extract of the deed is then published in the RESA on the official electronic legal gazette.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation (authentic form)
RCS application form signed by the Gérant
Statement of acceptance of office by the Gérant
Confirmation of paid-up capital release from the blocked account
Power of attorney to the notary for RCS filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query for missing documents, counsel supplies supplementary statutory declarations and clarifications within 15 days; if the registration is refused, the articles are amended by an extraordinary general meeting and a new notarial deed is executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, EORI and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) via Guichet.lu; Centre commun de la Sécurité sociale (CCSS); Business Data Luxembourg (BDL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the VAT registration form (formulaire 900-TVA) through Guichet.lu to obtain the Luxembourg VAT number (LU + 8 digits); apply for the EORI number for customs clearance of matcha imports from non-EU origins; register the Gérant and the company as employer with the CCSS; obtain the employer registration and accident insurance cover.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration and articles of incorporation
Proof of registered office address (lease deed or owner's written authorization)
Identification of the Gérant and shareholders
Application for EORI number
Bank account confirmation and financial statements projection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT requests physical evidence of office, supply a notarized lease or rent invoice; if CCSS contests the manager status, a formal shareholders' resolution on management remuneration is filed within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment permit and food-wholesale hygiene authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des classes moyennes (Direction de l'autorisation d'établissement); Administration luxembourgeoise vétérinaire et alimentaire (ALVA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online application for the business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) for wholesale trading activity corresponding to ISIC 4631. Concurrently file a food business operator (FBO) notification with ALVA under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004, describing the matcha powder warehousing, repacking and dispatch operations, and validating the HACCP system and traceability procedures.
required_dossiers: Standard application form for the establishment permit (Guichet.lu)
Extract of criminal record (bulletin n°3) of the Gérant
ALVA food premise notification and HACCP plan
Warehouse hygiene and temperature-control conformity certificate
Traceability procedure for organic matcha imports (EU-O certification)
Certificate of occupancy or municipality building clearance for the warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Economy questions the non-resident procurement model, file the suppliers' contracts and customs documentation; if ALVA raises allergen or cross-contamination concerns, submit an amended HACCP review and allergen-management plan within 15 working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des classes moyennes (Direction de l'autorisation d'établissement) in conjunction with the Administration luxembourgeoise vétérinaire et alimentaire (ALVA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Establishment Permit (autorisation d'établissement) for wholesale trading (ISIC 4631) and Food Business Operator approval (notification/agrément) under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full Environmental Impact Assessment; the activity is classified as Class 4 (general operation with no environmental statement). If warehousing exceeds 500 m² of storage area, a simple Class 3 commodo/incommodo declaration (déclaration préalable) may be required before the local commune.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are generated in matcha powder wholesale distribution; any repacking/labeling activity must comply with EU food-contact and hygiene material standards; waste registration under the Luxembourg Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management, plus annual waste declaration if non-hazardous waste exceeds 2 tonnes; wastewater discharges, if any, must meet the thresholds of the Law of 19 December 2008 on Water Management (no hazardous substances above legal limits).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) following structural inspection; building occupancy/fit-out clearance from the competent municipal commune; occupational safety and workplace hygiene approval from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM), including emergency exits, storage rack stability, electrical safety, and food-handling staff health certificates.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct corporate taxation; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT; national e-portal MyGuichet.lu and guichet.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign entity not established in Luxembourg, VAT registration is mandatory before any taxable supply if no local fixed establishment exists. The foreign SARL (or its VAT representative) must file Form 102 via MyGuichet.lu, attach statutory incorporation documents, proof of economic activity, and power of attorney if a fiscal representative is appointed. Upon approval, the AED issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number (LU + 8 digits) and a national business registration number is obtained from the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box regime. A SARL is automatically subject to entity-level corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax. Elective mechanisms include tax consolidation under Article 164 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR) for resident companies and the option to form a VAT group under specific conditions. Hybrid mismatch elections are constrained by EU ATAD provisions as transposed into Luxembourg law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For non-established foreign entities: no registration threshold (mandatory from the first taxable transaction). For resident small enterprises: annual turnover exemption threshold of EUR 35,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory for business-to-government contracts in Luxembourg under PEPPOL/EN 16931. There is no general real-time fiscal clearance, API-based invoice stamping, or continuous transaction control regime for B2B or export VAT. VAT returns must be filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu with periodicity determined by annual turnover.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations qualify for 0% VAT where the supplier or its agent proves that the goods were physically dispatched or transported outside the EU. Evidence must include a customs export declaration, transport documentation, commercial invoice, and, when relevant, proof of payment. Intra-EU supplies of matcha powder may also be zero-rated where the customer is VAT-registered and the goods are dispatched to another EU member state.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg VAT authorities may require evidence of export within 90 days of the supply and have power to reassess and claw back zero-rated treatment with statutory interest. False or unsupported export zero-rating claims are subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 10,000 per violation, criminal penalties including imprisonment for tax fraud, and full repayment of input VAT recovered on the underlying goods. Although no statutory foreign-currency repatriation deadline exists for VAT purposes, absence of an Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent banking proof is a documented audit red flag and may trigger detailed forensic review.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), the national central bank within the European System of Central Banks; the European Central Bank (ECB) exercises exclusive Eurosystem authority over monetary policy and official foreign-exchange operations. Financial-sector conduct and AML/CFT supervision are vested in the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg enforces no standalone foreign-exchange control law; cross-border capital movements are governed by the EU free-movement-of-capital regime (Articles 63–66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible, and Luxembourg maintains fully liberalized current and capital accounts with no administrative approval, licensing, or registration requirement for inbound equity injection, shareholder loans, trade settlement, or dividend/profit remittance. An SARL may freely receive and disburse EUR, USD, JPY, and other currencies through any CSSF-supervised credit institution. The only fiscal friction on outbound profit is Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (15% statutory; reduced to 0–5% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 2011/96/EU or applicable double-tax treaties). Statutory legal-reserve rules (allocation of 5% of annual net profit until the reserve reaches 10% of paid-up capital, pursuant to the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended) must be observed before any discretionary dividend distribution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg and the Eurozone impose no statutory surrender ratio, no repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion obligation for export proceeds. Receipts from matcha powder re-exports may be retained indefinitely in the settlement currency (EUR, USD, JPY, or other) in onshore or offshore accounts; the only requirement is statistical reporting of cross-border transactions to the BCL (effected by the domestic bank) under applicable ECB balance-of-payments regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow (compte bloqué) + Operational / Multi-currency Account
Operational Account + Commercial LC / Standby LC

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational collections/disbursements; Low for capital escrow and trade-finance instruments. CSSF-licensed payment institutions and electronic-money institutions (Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services as amended; CSSF Circulars 18/698 and 23/811) may lawfully provide multi-currency IBANs, virtual accounts, and FX conversion with client funds held in segregated safeguarding accounts. However, an EMI cannot issue documentary letters of credit, cannot deliver the notary-grade blocked-funds attestation (attestation de blocage) required for SARL incorporation, and is not an acceptable primary banking relationship for a distribution company; non-EU digital EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Revolut Business, Payoneer) are permissible only as supplementary collection rails, with settlement waterfalls directed to a tier-1 Luxembourg credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one authorized director (and the notary) is mandatory at incorporation and at the blocked-capital-account instruction. For standard operational account opening, a face-to-face KYC interview is de facto required by most tier-1 Luxembourg banks; remote video-KYC is conditionally accepted where the onboarding policy permits eIDAS-qualified electronic identification, notarized apostilled corporate documentation, and consular legalization for foreign signatories. A director resident outside the EU/EEA must either appear in person or execute a durable power of attorney before a Luxembourg notary or at a Luxembourg consulate, and all directors and UBOs over 25% must be identified and verified in accordance with CSSF Regulation 12-02 before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident (Luxembourg-external) shareholders or a multi-jurisdictional group with an opaque beneficial-ownership chain above the SARL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extract from the Luxembourg Register of Commerce (RCS); notarized articles of association; an updated group organigram disclosing every UBO holding more than 25%; registered extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) or reasoned confirmation of registration exemption; valid passports and proof of residential address for all directors and UBOs; and audited financial statements or bank references of the parent undertaking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border procurement from Japan/China with large advance payments for organic matcha powder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed supply agreements and pro-forma invoices; bills of lading or airway bills with marine/open-cargo insurance certificates; EU customs documentation (Single Administrative Document); JAS-organic and EU-organic import equivalence certificates; supplier KYC and sanctions-screening file; and a board-approved vendor-payment policy consistent with the declared wholesale distribution model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid deployment or outbound repatriation of injected share capital (treasury netting, immediate intercompany loans, or early dividend payment)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed and attestation de blocage; three-year cash-flow and liquidity plan; board resolutions authorizing the treasury policy; master intercompany agreements priced per OECD transfer-pricing principles; Luxembourg tax-residency certificate; and documentary evidence of real operational substance (warehousing, logistics contracts, purchase/sales ledgers, first-year stock movement).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media screening flags arising from name-alias matches in Asian supplier or counterparty identities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Output of a documented automated screening tool with fuzzy-matching logic; corporate extracts obtained from the relevant Asian corporate registries; a written explanation letter with nationality, date of birth, and address data affirmatively eliminating false-positive hits; completed UBO background verification; and, if required, an independent legal opinion from external counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Account turnover velocity or single-transaction size disproportionate to the declared low-risk matcha distribution margin
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Reconciliation of purchase orders, sales invoices, inventory movements, and VAT returns; customs clearance records; transport and insurance documentation; and a written goods-flow narrative (Japan → Luxembourg hub → EU/third-country customers) establishing that the SARL holds real inventory, bears commercial risk, and does not act as a pass-through shell.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The statutory share capital is wired via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the SARL's blocked capital account (compte bloqué) at a Luxembourg credit institution; field 77B (Regulatory Reporting) must state the EU/ECB balance-of-payments purpose category 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital', and the narrative must identify the contribution to the capitalization of 'LU_SARL' (ISIC 4631). The receiving bank issues an attestation de blocage to the notary confirming the funds are irrevocably paid up; the notary files the incorporation at the RCS; upon registration, the bank releases the funds to the operational account. Shareholder loans follow the same routing with purpose category 'Direct Investment – Loans between Related Enterprises' and a contemporaneous written loan agreement. The bank will screen the remitter and verify the UBO structure against the RBE/RCS registers before release.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for organic matcha powder settle via SWIFT MT103 (euro leg cleared through TARGET2 or EBA CLEARING's EURO1/STEP2) with 'Imports of Goods – Organic Matcha' stated as the purpose and the ECB BOP category 'Imports of Goods' recorded for statistical reporting; documentary commercial letters of credit are issued per SWIFT MT700 with MT707 amendments for high-value lots, and standby LCs (MT760) may be granted where suppliers require a payment undertaking. Euro-area treasury moves use SEPA Credit Transfer (and SEPA Instant where same-day settlement is required). All disbursements must be supported by transport, customs, and commercial documentation retained in the bank's transaction file, and FX conversion is executed against a board-approved treasury framework.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: European-style OTC foreign-exchange options (EUR/JPY and EUR/USD)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to non-convertible settlement currencies (e.g., onshore CNY) if regional supply-chain re-routing creates an unhedgeable convertibility exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) comprising balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, and notes, approved by the shareholders' general meeting and filed for publication with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing administrative fine of EUR 100–1,000; coercive daily fine (astreinte) of up to EUR 250 imposed by the District Court upon RCS referral; non-filing for three consecutive financial years exposes the SARL to judicial strike-off (radiation) from the RCS, loss of legal standing, and manager civil liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the beneficial-ownership (UBO) declaration confirming that recorded RBE data remains complete and accurate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once every 12 months from the last UBO declaration or confirmation; share-transfer-driven changes in beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of the SARL becoming aware of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines from EUR 250 to EUR 250,000 under the Law of 13 January 2019 as amended in 2024; persistent default is referred by the RBE registrar to the State Prosecutor; non-compliance can invalidate notarized share transfers and block bank account operations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual direct tax declaration package (Formulaire 720 e-file) covering corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax, including minimum net wealth tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 30 June of the following tax year for calendar-year SARLs; e-filed declarations are generally granted an extended window up to 31 December under ACD administrative practice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Tax increase (taxe d'office) of up to 10% of the assessed tax; monthly late-payment interest accrues on unpaid corporate income and municipal business tax; the ACD may estimate taxable basis ex officio and enforce by seizure, though tax default does not directly trigger RCS strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit by an approved réviseur d'entreprises is triggered where the SARL exceeds at least two of the three thresholds on two consecutive balance-sheet dates: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average workforce 50 employees; smaller SARLs are exempt from statutory audit, but shareholders holding 10% of the voting rights may petition for appointment of an auditor
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts, as amended, transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU and using the Plan comptable normalisé (PCN); IFRS is not mandatory for a non-listed trading SARL and is adopted only for optional consolidated reporting

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must update the RBE within one month of any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership and must thereafter log into the MyRBE portal at least once every 12 months to confirm that recorded UBO data is unchanged; annual confirmation is blocked while a pending amendment remains unfiled; the managing director certifies the declaration personally, and each identified beneficial owner must verify the data filed about them
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des parts sociales)
Register of Directors and Management Resolutions (Registre des gérants)
Minute Book of Shareholders' General Meetings and Board Decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,300-2,700 per annum for professional domiciliation, corporate agent, and registered-office services in Luxembourg City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000-25,000 per engagement for a certified réviseur d'entreprises audit of a mid-sized Luxembourg SARL

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), plus a 7% solidarity surcharge (adding 1.19 percentage points) and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal). The aggregate statutory headline rate for a Luxembourg City-registered SARL is 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent/innovation box: 80% of qualifying net IP income is exempt from CIT, yielding an effective rate of approximately 5.05% on such income; participation exemption: 100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains with a minimum 10% shareholding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost and a 12-month holding period; R&D tax credit of 20% on the first EUR 300,000 of qualifying R&D expenditure and 10% above, capped at EUR 1.5 million annually.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 760 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) covering CIT and municipal business tax, filed electronically via the eCDF (Electronic Corporate Declaration Filing) portal of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD). Form 763 is filed simultaneously for net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the fiscal year normally coincides with the calendar year. No quarterly corporate income tax filing obligation applies; quarterly instalments are limited to the VAT regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Form 760 return for tax year N must be filed by 31 December of year N+1; the ACD invitation letter ordinarily requires filing by 30 June of N+1 for calendar-year companies. Upon justified request, an electronic filing extension until 30 September may be granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company matricule number, RCS Number, tax office code and return-year indicator.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the ACD-issued matricule of the Luxembourg SARL; the non-resident shareholder identification is not entered in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SARL designation, registered office address and status as investment company or SOPARFI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Legal-form data only; no shareholder disclosure required at this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the accounting period subject to assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the year-end with the RCS annual filing; the foreign parent's fiscal year-end is irrelevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before tax as per the statutory financial statements prepared under Luxembourg GAAP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the SARL's separate statutory result only; do not consolidate the non-resident parent's figures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reintegration of fines, penalties, CIT and ICC themselves, non-commercial expenses and unjustified gifts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Hidden profit distributions such as excessive management fees paid to the foreign parent must be reintegrated into the taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 80% patent-box deduction on qualifying IP income and 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividend and capital-gain income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the shareholding track record, holding-period certificate and proof that the foreign parent is the ultimate beneficial owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year tax losses subject to the statutory cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the SARL's own loss history is usable; losses of the non-resident parent or affiliates are non-compensable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT at 17%, solidarity surcharge at 7% of CIT and municipal business tax at the communal rate (6.75% in Luxembourg City).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the communal rate of the SARL's registered office; income of the foreign shareholder is outside scope unless a Luxembourg permanent establishment exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% tax majoration plus default interest of 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum) on the outstanding tax. Ex officio assessment may add a surcharge of 10% to 100% of the tax due. Wilful late filing or false declaration is a criminal offence under the LIR with fines up to EUR 50,000 and potential imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% under Luxembourg domestic law. The rate is reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the corporate shareholder holds at least 10% of the SARL for at least 12 months; tax-treaty rates typically range from 0% to 15% depending on the residence state and holding percentage.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply the reduced or zero rate at source, the foreign shareholder must submit a valid tax residence certificate (certificat de résidence fiscale) issued by its tax authority, together with a beneficial-ownership declaration, to the Luxembourg paying agent before the dividend payment. If the statutory 15% is withheld, the beneficiary may reclaim the excess through the ACD refund procedure by filing the official refund claim with the TRC, share register extracts and holding-period evidence; the ACD processes claims for the relevant calendar year within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no withholding tax on outbound interest (0%) and no withholding tax on outbound royalties (0%) under domestic law. Tax treaties generally maintain the 0% rate; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive is available where a 25% or greater direct holding exists.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A statutory transfer-pricing documentation file must be maintained where aggregate annual cross-border transactions between the SARL and related parties exceed EUR 450,000. A Country-by-Country Report and corresponding Master File are required where the group's consolidated annual revenue is at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone Economic Substance Regulation regime as applied in zero-tax centres. Instead, economic substance is enforced through the general anti-abuse doctrine (abus de droit), the GAAR implementing ATAD, the participation-exemption substance conditions and the Principal Purpose Test embedded in Luxembourg's tax treaties. The SARL must demonstrate local substance through physical office premises, operational staff, board meetings held in Luxembourg, genuine decision-making and commercial activity commensurate with its matcha trading function; absence of such substance may trigger denial of treaty or directive benefits, recharacterization of transactions and reassessment under the arm's length standard.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully failing to file Form 760, concealing taxable income, inflating deductible expenses or submitting false financial statements to the ACD.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax increase of 10% to 100% of the evaded tax plus monthly default interest of 0.6%. Criminal conviction for tax fraud (Article 396 LIR) carries fines up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment of up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause the filing of false returns become personally liable for the evaded tax, civil restitution and criminal penalties; the ACD may issue against them personal tax enforcement orders, and the competent court may impose travel bans and arrest warrants during the criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SARL as a letterbox entity without real presence, decision-making or commercial activity, with the sole purpose of accessing treaty benefits or the participation exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty and EU Directive benefits, disallowance of the participation exemption, recharacterization of the structure under the GAAR and abuse-of-law doctrine, and reassessment of the full income with 0.6% monthly interest and surcharges up to 100%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: De facto and de jure directors may be held jointly liable for the additional corporate tax liabilities when they knowingly implemented the artificial structure; disqualification from board mandates and criminal exposure for aiding tax evasion may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register the beneficial owner in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), or omitting the non-resident shareholder from the RBE filing, including falsifying the economic-substance declaration for AML/KYC purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the law of 13 January 2019 ranging up to EUR 1.25 million for legal persons; the commercial court may suspend the SARL's activity; CSSF and banking partners may freeze payment rails and terminate banking relationships.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally subject to fines of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of up to two years for deliberate non-compliance; in addition, directors can be ordered by the court to remedy the registration under penalty payments per day of delay.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Hidden Profit Distribution and Undisclosed Dividend
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying gratuitous benefits, excessive management fees or interest-free shareholder loans from the SARL to the non-resident shareholder, or distributing profits without recording a dividend and without withholding the statutory 15% WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the payment as a constructive dividend subject to 15% withholding tax plus default interest of 0.6% per month; the SARL may be assessed as agent for the uncollected WHT; the shareholder payment loses deductibility and attracts tax increases of up to 100%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the unremitted withholding tax where they knowingly arranged the undisclosed distribution; liability extends to civil restitution to the tax authority, and criminal sanctions under Article 396 LIR including fines and imprisonment up to five years.
